question: Which of these is NOT a safe safety practice in the operating room?

options.D: Recapping used injection needles by hand before disposal

question: A patient cannot afford expensive imported foods listed on a standard diet sheet. What should you do as their nurse?

options.A: Tell them to stop worrying about nutrition and just eat less food
options.B: Discharge the patient without any dietary plan
options.C: Suggest nutritious, affordable, and culturally familiar local food alternatives
options.D: Insist that they find extra money to buy the prescribed imported items

explanation: Great nursing judgment! Always adapt care to fit the patient's pocket by recommending budget-friendly, local Nigerian food options. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T014#GNS227_U4_T014_h5)

question: When do program evaluations usually take place during a health project's lifecycle?

options.A: Every single morning during the nurse handover briefing
options.B: At specific milestones, such as midterm and project completion
options.C: Randomly without any set schedule or plan
options.D: Only after funding has completely run out and staff have left

explanation: Evaluations are scheduled check-ins at key points (like midway or at the end) to see how well the project is doing. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T21#GNS225_U2_T21_h5)

question: Why do doctors usually prescribe SSRIs instead of benzodiazepines for daily, long-term anxiety management?

options.A: SSRIs stop panic attacks within two minutes of taking the pill.
options.B: SSRIs treat underlying chronic anxiety safely over time without addiction risks.
options.C: SSRIs have zero side effects compared to other psychiatric drugs.
options.D: Benzodiazepines cause permanent brain damage in every patient.

explanation: You got it! SSRIs are much safer for everyday, long-term use because they manage anxiety steadily without the trap of physical addiction. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T5#GNS314_U2_T5_h6)

question: What are the two main parts that make up a patient's overall level of consciousness?

options.A: Speech and memory
options.B: Reflexes and coordination
options.C: Arousal and awareness
options.D: Strength and sensation

explanation: Consciousness is all about being awake (arousal) and being able to interact with your surroundings and thoughts (awareness). Both are essential! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T20#GNS222_U3_T20_h2)

question: What is the main goal of outpatient nutritional care?

options.A: Treating acute malnutrition only inside intensive care units
options.B: Helping clients manage their diet while living independently
options.C: Controlling all daily meal preparations in a facility
options.D: Prescribing complex surgical interventions for obesity

explanation: You've got this! Outpatient care focuses on helping people who live at home make healthy food choices on their own. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T002#GNS227_U3_T002_h1)

question: Why do patients receiving home care require different types of nursing care plans?

options.A: Because insurance companies refuse to pay for identical nursing tasks
options.B: Because a surgery recovery patient has different daily needs than someone with chronic heart failure
options.C: Because hospital policies dictate what happens inside private homes
options.D: Because every single patient shares the exact same medical diagnosis

explanation: Different health conditions require distinct nursing goals, monitoring schedules, and treatment approaches. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T8#GNS324_U1_T8_h1)

question: Why do we apply heavy oil or petroleum jelly over a skin boil that has a fly larva inside?

options.A: To dissolve the outer skin layer and make surgical cutting unnecessary
options.B: To cool down the local inflammation and numb the severe pain instantly
options.C: To block the breathing hole and force the larva to crawl out for air
options.D: To poison the parasite with chemical toxins absorbed through its skin

explanation: Smothering the breathing hole cuts off their oxygen supply, tricking the larva into crawling out where you can safely remove it. Clever nursing trick! [learn more](GST114_U3_T7#GST114_U3_T7_h6)

question: What is the typical acid-base blood gas state during a normal pregnancy?

options.A: Acute metabolic alkalosis
options.B: Uncompensated metabolic acidosis
options.C: Severe respiratory acidosis
options.D: Compensated respiratory alkalosis

explanation: Mums breathe off extra carbon dioxide, leading to mild respiratory alkalosis which the kidneys smoothly balance out with bicarbonate. Great revision! [learn more](GNS121_U7_T3#GNS121_U7_T3_h4)

question: What is the most critical check a nurse must do before giving penicillin for the first time?

options.A: Measuring the patient head circumference
options.B: Checking for a history of drug allergies
options.C: Evaluating the patient visual acuity score
options.D: Assessing the patient daily fluid intake

explanation: Safety first! Always check for allergies. A patient with a severe penicillin allergy can crash quickly from anaphylaxis if you miss this step. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T4#GNS223_U2_T4_h5)

question: Which chemical messenger is blocked by anticholinergic anti-spasmodics to stop cramps?

options.A: Acetylcholine
options.B: Epinephrine
options.C: Serotonin
options.D: Dopamine

explanation: Acetylcholine is the chemical messenger that tells your gut muscles to squeeze. Anticholinergics step in to block it, helping the muscles finally relax. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T4#GNS223_U3_T4_h2)

question: If a patient is given a new drug classed as an antihypertensive, what main effect should you expect?

options.A: Elevated blood glucose
options.B: Reduced joint inflammation
options.C: Increased bacterial cell death
options.D: Lowered blood pressure

explanation: Well done! 'Anti' means against, and 'hypertensive' refers to high blood pressure—so antihypertensives bring high blood pressure down. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T3#GNS125_U1_T3_h4)

question: What does 'bivariate data' mean when working on a nursing research project?

options.A: Measurements are taken twice on the same patient
options.B: Two different variables are collected from each subject
options.C: Two researchers analyze the same set of numbers
options.D: Data is gathered from two separate hospitals at once

explanation: Bivariate just means two pieces of information (like a patient's age and their blood pressure) are gathered from each person. Easy peasy! [learn more](GNS217_U4_T12#GNS217_U4_T12_h1)

question: What is the main difference in how drug treatment is chosen for type 1 versus type 2 diabetes?

options.A: Type 1 is managed strictly through lifestyle changes without drugs
options.B: Type 2 patients never need insulin under any clinical circumstances
options.C: Type 2 can only be treated with injectable non-insulin medications
options.D: Type 1 always requires insulin, while type 2 often starts with oral agents

explanation: Well done! Because type 1 diabetes means the body doesn't make insulin at all, replacement therapy is needed right from the start. [learn more](GNS223_U7_T1#GNS223_U7_T1_h2)

question: Why do different organizational cultures, such as military versus humanitarian groups, cause friction in a response?

options.A: They operate under conflicting leadership styles and operational rules
options.B: Humanitarian workers refuse to wear protective boots
options.C: They are legally forbidden from speaking to one another in public
options.D: They always use completely different spoken languages

explanation: Rigid military hierarchies and flexible volunteer groups often clash over how decisions should be made in the field. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T7#GNS315_U5_T7_h7)

question: When a severe flood hits a local community, the local Red Cross branch rushes in to set up emergency shelters. What do we call this local branch?

options.A: The ICRC leadership
options.B: A United Nations agency
options.C: A National Society
options.D: A military medical unit

explanation: Spot on! National Societies work right inside their own countries, stepping up as local heroes when disasters strike. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T10#GNS315_U1_T10_h4)

question: Which of these is an example of structural mitigation in a hospital?

options.A: Teaching community members how to wash their hands
options.B: Bolting heavy oxygen tanks securely to the wall

options.D: Conducting a fire drill for the nursing staff

question: Why is it important to teach family members how to spot early warning signs?

options.A: Family members are qualified to prescribe psychiatric drugs

options.D: Family members live with the patient and can spot changes early

question: Why is working closely with local and religious leaders so vital for successful immunization drives?

options.A: Village leaders are trained to administer routine injections during staff shortages
options.B: Community members fund the importation of foreign vaccine supplies
options.C: Trusted local voices help address fears and clear up cultural misconceptions about vaccines
options.D: Local leaders inspect refrigerator temperatures every morning before clinic opens

explanation: People trust their community leaders. When elders and local leaders support immunization, families feel safe and eager to bring their children forward! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T70#GNS214_U1_T70_h8)

question: Under the WHO medical rules, what does a Category 4 classification mean for a contraceptive method?

options.A: The benefits outweigh the risks in most cases
options.B: There are no restrictions on using the method
options.C: The method can be used with routine monitoring
options.D: The method represents an unacceptable health risk

explanation: Category 4 means 'Stop!' — the condition is too dangerous, and the contraceptive must not be used because it puts the client's health at serious risk. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T013#GNS226_U6_T013_h3)

question: What is the main difference between monitoring and evaluation in a project?

options.A: Monitoring happens after the project ends, while evaluation happens before it starts.
options.B: Monitoring deals with money, while evaluation deals strictly with medicines.
options.C: Monitoring is done by the community, while evaluation is done by politicians.
options.D: Monitoring tracks activities during implementation, while evaluation measures final impact.

explanation: Spot on! Monitoring is what you do while the work is going on, while evaluation checks the final results after everything is done. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T2#GNS214_U1_T2_h6)

question: What is the main goal when a patient arrives in the emergency department?

options.A: To provide long-term rehabilitation therapy
options.B: To discharge patients within a strict time limit
options.C: To complete detailed medical histories for all patients
options.D: To stabilize life-threatening conditions swiftly

explanation: Spot on! In emergency nursing, the absolute priority is making sure the patient stays alive and stable before worrying about anything else. You're doing great! [learn more](GNS315_U1_T4#GNS315_U1_T4_h1)

question: Which patient sensation is commonly reported immediately after receiving a fast IV push of adenosine?

options.A: Severe numbness and tingling in both legs and feet
options.B: A brief feeling of the heart pausing or chest pressure
options.C: Sudden uncontrollable shaking in the hands and arms
options.D: An intense craving for cold water and sweet foods

question: A community health nurse organizes a blood pressure screening in the marketplace. What level of prevention is this?

options.D: Terminal prevention

question: What is a reservoir in the chain of infection?

options.A: The method used by a microbe to travel to a new host
options.B: The natural habitat where a pathogen lives and multiplies
options.C: The specific entry point through broken skin
options.D: A person who has complete immunity against disease

explanation: A reservoir acts as the home base where germs live, grow, and reproduce before moving to a new host. [learn more](GST114_U1_T3#GST114_U1_T3_h2)

question: Why is studying an entire population usually impractical for a nursing study?

options.A: Research ethics committees do not allow large studies
options.B: Patients refuse to answer questions if everyone is included
options.C: Statistical software cannot process large amounts of data
options.D: It is too expensive, time-consuming, and logistically difficult

question: Why is changing or back-dating a patient's chart after a bad incident a serious offense?

options.C: It destroys the legal integrity and truthfulness of the clinical record
options.D: It prevents the electronic health record from backing up data

question: Why must a waiting patient be reassessed periodically in the emergency department?

options.A: Nurses need to practice their physical assessment skills

options.D: It prevents patients from leaving without paying

question: What does motivation mean in a healthcare workplace?

options.C: The mandatory number of clinical hours a nurse works each week
options.D: The strict enforcement of hospital policies by upper management

question: Why is writing a detailed clinical history on the lab form so important when sending off a skin biopsy?

options.A: It determines how much money the laboratory will bill the patient's insurance

question: What is the name of the suture that separates the two parietal bones along the top of the fetal head?

question: You need to scan patient bands and check medications right at the bedside using a portable device. Which computer type do you grab?

question: Why are midwives particularly vital in Nigeria's primary health care system?

question: Which simple tool do nurses use right in the field to quickly check if a child is suffering from malnutrition?

question: What happens inside the body during disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC)?

options.A: Widespread clotting exhausts platelets and factors, causing severe bleeding.

options.C: Vitamin K is completely destroyed in the stomach.
options.D: Platelets permanently lose their ability to stick together.

question: How does a vasectomy change a man's semen volume after surgery?

question: How do residential care homes differ basically from nursing homes?

options.C: Residential care homes are exclusively for children, whereas nursing homes are strictly for the elderly

question: A nurse assumes an older patient with confusion simply has baseline dementia, without checking for a new urinary tract infection. Which cognitive trap is this?

options.D: Confirmation bias

question: Why do we perform passive range of motion exercises for a paralyzed patient?

question: What is the underlying physiological problem in all types of shock?

question: A doctor dismisses your drug dose warning with sarcasm. What should you do next as an assertive nurse?

question: What is a common psychological consequence experienced by individuals with faecal incontinence?

question: Which germ causes leprosy?

question: What is the primary focus of clinical nursing informatics?

question: What is a common daily challenge for clinical nurses who want to get involved in research?

question: A mother looks anxious and confused about why her baby needs multiple injections. As a nurse, what is your best approach?

question: What is the main focus during the pre-survey phase of a community diagnosis?

question: Why do health problems after a disaster often last a very long time?

question: When cleaning a patient's skin before surgery, what is the correct way to apply the antiseptic solution?

question: What is a key role of the community nurse when a family needs financial or social help?

question: Why is proper management of healthcare resources so important on the ward?

options.D: It eliminates the need for any nursing documentation

question: What is the normal baseline range for a baby's heart rate during labor?

question: What does a 24-hour dietary recall ask the patient to do?

question: Which ethical principle refers to the nurse's core duty to do no harm to patients?

question: What color is the sputum typically seen in a patient with a lung fluke infection?

question: What is a common operational challenge faced by nurses in Nigerian primary health care centers?

question: What is the primary stimulus that causes the kidneys to release erythropoietin (EPO)?

question: A patient is brought to the emergency unit looking very restless, sweating profusely, and with a racing heart after taking an unknown substance. Which drug class is likely to blame?

options.C: Barbiturates

question: Which of these skin conditions needs careful medical evaluation rather than just reassurance?

question: Which group of viruses is most commonly spread through contaminated injection equipment?

options.A: Respiratory viruses like Influenza and the common cold
options.B: Fungal spores that cause superficial skin rashes
options.C: Intestinal parasites spread through contaminated water
options.D: Blood-borne pathogens like Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C, and HIV

explanation: Because unsafe injections often transfer tiny amounts of blood between people, blood-borne viruses are our biggest concern in clinical safety. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T3#GNS122_U4_T3_h4)

question: Which of these is a classic example of a Clinical Decision Support System in action?

options.A: The computer screen automatically dims to save electricity during night shift hours
options.B: An email reminder is sent to the nurse manager about an upcoming staff meeting
options.C: A pop-up warning appears on the screen noting that a newly ordered drug conflicts with a patient allergy
options.D: A printer in the nurse's station prints out the morning breakfast menu list

explanation: Spot on! Drug-allergy alerts are a great example of CDSS protecting patients by catching potential mistakes before they reach the bedside. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T4#GNS113_U1_T4_h5)

question: In which part of the female reproductive tract does fertilization usually take place?

options.A: Body of the uterus
options.B: Cervical canal
options.C: Ampulla of the fallopian tube
options.D: Ovarian cortex

explanation: Spot on! The ampulla is the wider section of the fallopian tube where the sperm and egg love to finally meet and fuse. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T8#GNS121_U5_T8_h1)

question: What does drug non-compliance mean in nursing practice?

options.A: A doctor writing an illegible prescription slip
options.B: A nurse administering the wrong dose of medication
options.C: A pharmacy running out of essential prescribed drugs
options.D: A patient failing to follow a prescribed medication regimen

explanation: Non-compliance simply means the patient is not taking their drugs the way the doctor or nurse instructed them to. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T5#GNS215_U4_T5_h1)

question: Why is keeping an eye on chronic health conditions so important during post-abortion care?

options.A: It guarantees immediate fertility restoration
options.B: It prevents minor issues from becoming emergencies
options.C: It eliminates the need for pain medication
options.D: It reduces hospital administrative costs

explanation: Spotting and managing chronic diseases early stops them from flaring up and getting worse during a time when the body is under physical stress. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T017#GNS226_U5_T017_h1)

question: Why is asking about a patient's job so important during a health assessment?

options.A: It proves the employer is legally guilty of negligence
options.B: It determines the exact salary the worker earns each month
options.C: It replaces the need for standard physical examinations
options.D: It links patient symptoms to exposures in their workplace

explanation: Many illnesses build up slowly over time. Knowing what a patient does for a living helps us connect the dots to their health issues. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T6#GNS225_U7_T6_h6)

question: Why can a poorly designed computer screen or software interface become a safety hazard for patients?

options.A: It distracts nurses from spending time with patients
options.B: It drains the hospital battery backup systems too quickly
options.C: It slows down internet speeds across the entire clinic
options.D: It increases the financial cost of buying hardware

explanation: Spot on! When software is clumsy and hard to navigate, nurses waste precious time fighting with menus instead of focusing on direct patient care. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T2#GNS113_U3_T2_h1)

question: Why is community participation important for making public health spending more transparent?

options.A: It empowers local citizens to hold health authorities accountable for funds
options.B: It removes the need for trained accountants in hospitals
options.C: It allows villagers to write the national health budget themselves
options.D: It guarantees that private clinics will lower their drug prices

explanation: When the local community is involved, they can ask questions and make sure that money meant for their local clinic actually gets used there. [learn more](GST322_U3_T3#GST322_U3_T3_h8)

question: What is the normal healthy pH range for human blood?
explanation: Keep this number in your pocket—a blood pH of 7.35 to 7.45 is a vital sign range that the lungs and kidneys work hard to maintain every single day. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T7#GNS121_U2_T7_h3)

question: Which type of graph is best suited for showing continuous data tracked over time?

options.A: Scatter table
options.B: Line graph
options.C: Demographic matrix
options.D: Pie chart

explanation: Line graphs are specifically designed to illustrate trends and changes across sequential time points. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T4#GNS224_U2_T4_h4)

question: Nursing informatics is a cool blend of three major fields. Which ones make up this specialty?

options.A: Biology, chemistry, and health administration
options.B: Nursing science, computer science, and information science
options.C: Nursing theory, public health, and data analytics
options.D: Pharmacology, anatomy, and computer engineering

explanation: Spot on! Nursing informatics brings together nursing science, computer science, and information science to help us manage health data like pros. You'll see this tech in action everywhere on the wards! [learn more](GNS113_U1_T3#GNS113_U1_T3_h1)

question: Why is Guinea worm disease such a big problem for farming villages?

options.A: It causes long-term cognitive impairment in infected adults
options.B: It kills most infected working-age adults within weeks
options.C: It destroys livestock and crops stored in the village
options.D: It inflicts crippling pain that stops people from farming

explanation: Spot on! The intense pain makes it hard to walk or work, which hits farming communities hard during harvest season. You're building solid public health sense! [learn more](GNS313_U2_T23#GNS313_U2_T23_h1)

question: A patient is due for their blood pressure medication, but their current BP is down to 85/50 mmHg. What should you do first?

options.A: Hold the medication and notify the physician
options.B: Give the drug with a large glass of water
options.C: Proceed with the dose as ordered on the chart
options.D: Administer half the dose to be safe

explanation: Their blood pressure is already on the lower side! Giving a BP-lowering drug now could cause dangerous crashing, so hold the dose and tell the doctor. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T2#GNS125_U3_T2_h3)

question: What does emotional health really mean for a person?

options.A: Having a high intelligence quotient
options.B: A dynamic state of coping with life and realizing one's potential
options.C: The total absence of any stressful life events
options.D: Always feeling happy and joyful throughout the day

explanation: Emotional health isn't about being happy 24/7 or having zero stress. It's about balance, bouncing back from normal life challenges, and functioning well! [learn more](GNS314_U1_T5#GNS314_U1_T5_h1)

question: What is the main goal of home health care?

options.A: To provide permanent housing for chronically ill elderly citizens
options.B: To train family members to take over all doctor responsibilities
options.C: To deliver professional nursing and medical services directly to a patient's residence
options.D: To completely replace the need for emergency room visits during major trauma

explanation: Spot on! Home health care brings clinical nursing straight to the patient's doorstep to help them heal comfortably where they live. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h1)

question: What pregnancy hormone is most closely linked to the timing of first-trimester nausea and vomiting?

options.A: Human chorionic gonadotropin
options.B: Follicle stimulating hormone
options.C: Thyroid stimulating hormone
options.D: Luteinizing hormone

explanation: Human chorionic gonadotropin peaks during the first trimester right when nausea and vomiting are usually at their worst. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T012#GNS226_U2_T012_h1)

question: When do modern recovery guidelines generally suggest starting food by mouth after surgery?

options.A: Only after 48 hours of complete fasting
options.B: Within hours of waking from anesthesia
options.C: After waiting for active bowel sounds
options.D: Only after the patient passes flatus

explanation: Spot on! Feeding patients early is safe and actually helps their bowels wake up faster than starving them for days. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T009#GNS227_U7_T009_h4)

question: A patient taking a daily anticoagulant medication reports finding dark, tarry stools. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: A normal reaction to eating green leafy vegetables
options.B: Rapid dehydration due to warm weather conditions
options.C: Bleeding somewhere in the upper gastrointestinal tract
options.D: An infection caused by low white blood cell counts

explanation: Dark, tarry stools indicate digested blood coming from the stomach or upper gut, which is a sign of bleeding caused by anticoagulants. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T15#GNS311_U2_T15_h6)

question: Why is tracking vital sign trends more helpful than relying on a single set of numbers?

options.A: It is required by hospital insurance companies for billing purposes
options.B: It stops the nursing staff from having to check the patient repeatedly
options.C: It proves that the electronic monitor is calibrated correctly
options.D: It shows whether the patient's condition is improving or getting worse over time

explanation: A single number only tells you what is happening right now, whereas tracking numbers over time reveals the direction the patient is heading. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T9#GNS315_U3_T9_h6)

question: What is the main goal when medical help arrives immediately after a disaster?

options.A: To minimize death and illness
options.B: To train local volunteers
options.C: To rebuild damaged hospitals
options.D: To document insurance claims

explanation: You've got this! When disaster strikes, the immediate focus is always on saving lives and stopping severe illness through quick medical action. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T4#GNS315_U5_T4_h1)

question: In research, what does the 'validity' of a questionnaire mean?

options.A: Whether the tool can be completed in under ten minutes
options.B: Whether the tool measures what it is intended to measure
options.C: Whether the tool was printed on approved institutional paper
options.D: Whether the tool gives the exact same scores on repeat testing

explanation: Validity checks if your questions are truly capturing the specific concept or variable you set out to study. You're building solid clinical research skills! [learn more](GNS224_U1_T22#GNS224_U1_T22_h4)

question: What is the main job of antibiotics in our bodies?

options.A: To treat and manage bacterial infections
options.B: To boost overall red blood cell counts
options.C: To replace lost fluids and electrolytes
options.D: To lower elevated body temperature rapidly

explanation: You got this! Antibiotics are specifically made to hunt down and stop bacteria from causing trouble in the body. They don't touch viruses or fever on their own! [learn more](GNS223_U2_T4#GNS223_U2_T4_h1)

question: What type of white blood cell primarily produces antibodies?

options.A: Plasma cells
options.B: Platelets
options.C: Killer T-cells
options.D: Red blood cells

explanation: Plasma cells develop from B-lymphocytes and are the specialized cells that mass-produce and secrete antibodies into body fluids. [learn more](GST114_U4_T3#GST114_U4_T3_h1)

question: What is a potential long-term complication for an infant who survives a severe intracranial hemorrhage?

options.A: Developmental delays and seizure disorders
options.B: Early closure of all body joints
options.C: Permanent loss of the sense of smell only
options.D: Enlargement of the hands and feet

explanation: Significant bleeding inside the cranium can damage brain tissue, leading to chronic neurological issues like seizures and delayed milestones. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T16#GNS121_U6_T16_h6)

question: How does drying (dehydration) primarily preserve food?

options.A: By keeping the food at freezing cold temperatures
options.B: By increasing the internal oxygen levels of the food
options.C: By adding large amounts of chemical preservatives
options.D: By removing the water that microorganisms need to grow

explanation: Think of it this way: germs need water to survive and multiply, just like we do. Take the water away, and they can't grow! [learn more](GNS227_U3_T011#GNS227_U3_T011_h2)

question: Why do clinics with flexible operating hours attract more adolescent clients?

options.A: Medical supplies are cheaper to buy at night
options.B: Government regulations require 24-hour youth attendance
options.C: Teenagers can visit without missing school classes or exams
options.D: Staff members prefer working late evening hours

explanation: Flexible schedules remove major roadblocks, making it easy for students to take care of their health without disrupting their studies. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T18#GNS312_U3_T18_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT an environmental barrier to a nursing student's learning?

options.A: Extreme tiredness from a packed school timetable
options.B: Too much noise and overcrowded lecture halls
options.C: Helpful clinical preceptors and useful feedback
options.D: Not having enough basic medical training equipment

explanation: Supportive preceptors help you grow! Noise, shortages, and exhaustion are the real barriers that hold you back. [learn more](GST321_U8_T3#GST321_U8_T3_h7)

question: Which collaborative platform is most commonly integrated directly into secure hospital software systems?

options.A: Public social networks
options.B: Standard text messaging
options.C: Personal email accounts
options.D: Microsoft Teams

explanation: Microsoft Teams is built to integrate smoothly with enterprise healthcare software for secure internal communication and file sharing. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T5#GNS113_U3_T5_h4)

question: A community health nurse notices a high prevalence of type 2 diabetes in a specific neighborhood. What is the most appropriate action?

options.A: Close all local clinics since the population is already quite sick
options.B: Establish targeted screening and lifestyle education posts in that neighborhood
options.C: Transfer all affected patients immediately to a tertiary teaching hospital
options.D: Ignore the data because prevalence only matters for infectious outbreaks

explanation: High prevalence guides nurses to focus local resources, screening, and education where the need is greatest. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T12#GNS313_U1_T12_h6)

question: When might a doctor perform a procedure like a D&C (dilatation and curettage) for a patient with endometritis?

options.A: When retained products of conception are present in the uterus
options.B: When the white blood cell count returns to normal
options.C: When the patient develops a mild skin rash
options.D: When the patient refuses to take oral medications

explanation: If tiny bits of the placenta are left behind, they act like food for bacteria. A D&C helps clean out that leftover tissue so the infection can finally heal. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T20#GNS216_U5_T20_h6)

question: What is the primary focus of modern occupational health nursing?

options.A: Promoting and protecting worker well-being
options.B: Providing long-term hospital bedside care
options.C: Designing factory machinery and tools
options.D: Managing corporate financial portfolios

explanation: Occupational health nursing centers on safeguarding the health, safety, and overall well-being of employees across various work environments. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T2#GNS225_U7_T2_h1)

question: Why must a nurse pull back the clothes and actually look at the patient's bare chest during a breathing assessment?

options.A: To listen for tummy sounds in the chest
options.B: To check the exact skin temperature
options.C: To check for chest symmetry, injuries, and odd movements
options.D: To get the skin ready for ECG stickers

explanation: Exactly! Looking closely helps you spot uneven chest rise, hidden wounds, or flail segments that make breathing difficult. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T4#GNS315_U3_T4_h3)

question: Which question type is best for encouraging a patient to tell their story in their own words?

options.A: Closed-ended questions
options.B: Multiple-choice questions
options.C: Leading questions
options.D: Open-ended questions

explanation: Open-ended questions allow patients to elaborate freely without limiting their responses to a single word. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T2#GNS123_U2_T2_h2)

question: What makes a person's blood type classified as Rh-positive?

options.A: The lack of any proteins on the cell surface
options.B: The presence of anti-Rh antibodies in the plasma
options.C: The presence of the D antigen on red blood cells
options.D: The ability to donate blood to anyone safely

explanation: The main determinant of Rh-positive status is finding the D antigen on the surface of the red blood cells. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T2#GNS111_U2_T2_h3)

question: What test is always needed to give a 100% definitive diagnosis of cancer?

options.A: Tissue biopsy
options.B: Complete blood count
options.C: Magnetic resonance imaging
options.D: Ultrasound scan

explanation: Scans and blood tests give us great clues, but looking at a tiny tissue sample under a microscope is what confirms cancer for sure. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T15#GNS324_U4_T15_h5)

question: A hospital management wants to check if nurses are keeping proper wound care records. What should they do?

options.A: Increasing the number of night shifts for junior nurses
options.B: Transferring patients with wounds to a different facility
options.C: Organizing a social party for all the nursing staff
options.D: Conducting a nursing audit of surgical ward case notes

explanation: Exactly! Reviewing actual clinical charts through an audit gives clear proof of how well wound care is being documented and performed. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h2)

question: What is a primary goal of psychoeducation delivered during a home visit?

options.A: Removing all stressful events from the neighborhood completely
options.B: Teaching the client how to prescribe their own medications
options.C: Helping the client and family understand the illness and treatment
options.D: Convincing the family to move the client into a permanent asylum

explanation: Psychoeducation empowers the client and family with knowledge about symptoms, triggers, and the importance of treatment adherence. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T6#GNS314_U4_T6_h5)

question: How is 'appropriate technology' defined in Primary Health Care?

options.A: Traditional herbal remedies that have never been scientifically tested
options.B: The most expensive and advanced medical machinery available on the global market
options.C: Digital computer systems used exclusively in large urban teaching hospitals
options.D: Equipment and methods that are scientifically valid, affordable, and locally maintainable

explanation: Spot on! Appropriate technology hits the sweet spot: it actually works scientifically, but it is also cheap and easy for the local community to manage. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T3#GNS124_U1_T3_h5)

question: Why is connecting a patient to community resources like vocational training important?

options.A: It forces them to work without getting any rest
options.B: It ensures the clinic makes a financial profit
options.C: It replaces the need for talking to a nurse or doctor
options.D: It helps them regain independence and purpose through meaningful activity

explanation: Community resources like job training help patients reintegrate into society and build a fulfilling life after illness. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h7)

question: When MUST you use soap and water instead of an alcohol hand rub?

options.A: Immediately after removing clean, non-sterile examination gloves
options.B: Before taking a patient's routine blood pressure reading
options.C: When entering a patient room for a brief verbal assessment
options.D: When hands are visibly soiled with dirt or body fluids

explanation: Spot on! If your hands have visible dirt, blood, or body fluids on them, alcohol rubs just won't cut it. You need good old soap and water to physically wash the mess away. [learn more](GST114_U2_T21#GST114_U2_T21_h2)

question: Why should nurses understand how different healthcare sectors work?

options.A: It gives them the authority to open private pharmacies
options.B: It allows them to manage the hospital budget directly
options.C: It exempts them from clinical documentation duties
options.D: It helps them navigate patient referrals and financial barriers

explanation: As a nurse, you'll often guide patients through complex health systems. Knowing your way around different sectors makes discharge planning and referrals much smoother. [learn more](GST322_U5_T3#GST322_U5_T3_h1)

question: Which type of medication is usually the first choice for treating post-abortion cramps?

options.A: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs
options.B: Broad-spectrum oral antibiotics
options.C: Strong narcotic opioid analgesics
options.D: Central nervous system stimulants

explanation: NSAIDs like ibuprofen block prostaglandins, making them absolute superstars for tackling uterine cramps. Well done! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T014#GNS226_U5_T014_h3)

question: What is the best way for nurses to physically handle needles during a count?

options.A: Glance quickly over the tray from a distance
options.B: Count only the full packs without opening them
options.C: Let the surgeon handle the items alone
options.D: Point to or touch each item individually as it is counted

explanation: You've got it! Touching or pointing to each item helps ensure nothing gets skipped. Safety first! [learn more](GNS123_U5_T8#GNS123_U5_T8_h4)

question: Which body organ is mainly responsible for breaking down (metabolizing) most drugs?

options.A: The liver
options.B: The pancreas
options.C: The stomach
options.D: The kidneys

explanation: The liver is our body's main chemical processing factory! It handles most drug breakdown using special helper proteins called enzymes. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T9#GNS125_U5_T9_h2)

question: What is the name of the tough, outermost protective layer that wraps around a whole spinal nerve?

options.A: Meninges
options.B: Epineurium
options.C: Perineurium
options.D: Endoneurium

explanation: The epineurium acts like a sturdy outer jacket holding all the nerve fibers safely together as one big spinal nerve. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T26#GNS211_U3_T26_h2)

question: Which famous nursing theorist built her work around the patient's ability to perform self-care?

options.A: Callista Roy
options.B: Florence Nightingale
options.C: Dorothea Orem
options.D: Madeleine Leininger

explanation: Correct! Dorothea Orem's Self-Care Deficit Theory focuses on stepping in to help patients when they cannot manage their own self-care. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T12#GNS217_U3_T12_h4)

question: During a building collapse, you find a victim who is not breathing. You open their airway, but they still don't breathe. What color tag do you give them?

options.A: Yellow
options.B: Red
options.C: Black
options.D: Green

explanation: You got it. Under START triage, if someone remains breathless even after clearing the airway, they are tagged black (expectant) so limited resources can go to those who can be saved. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T2#GNS315_U1_T2_h5)

question: Why did ancient people use fermentation for baking and brewing long before anyone discovered microbes?

options.A: They followed strict written instructions left by early microbiologists
options.B: They observed the practical results of microbial action without knowing the cause
options.C: They accidentally stumbled upon chemicals that preserved food permanently
options.D: They possessed advanced microscopes made of polished river stones

explanation: Ancient folks didn't know about germs yet, but they knew bread dough rises and palm wine ferments through trial and observation! Great job. [learn more](GST114_U1_T2#GST114_U1_T2_h1)

question: Which laboratory blood test is considered the most reliable routine marker for estimating the Glomerular Filtration Rate?

options.A: Serum creatinine
options.B: Total serum protein
options.C: Serum potassium
options.D: White blood cell count

explanation: Creatinine levels rise when kidney filtration slows down, making it the standard lab marker for evaluating renal function. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T1#GNS121_U2_T1_h7)

question: In research language, what is a 'sampling frame'?

options.A: A framework for writing up the final research report
options.B: The physical room where patient interviews take place
options.C: A complete list of everyone in the accessible population
options.D: The statistical formula used to calculate sample size

explanation: Think of a sampling frame as your phone book or registry list. It's the actual directory of names you draw your participants from! [learn more](GNS224_U1_T16#GNS224_U1_T16_h4)

question: Which physical sign do nurses check first to quickly spot possible anaemia?

options.A: Swelling in the upper eyelids
options.B: Yellow color in the eyes
options.C: Pallor of the inner eyelids and nail beds
options.D: Dryness of the outer ears

explanation: Looking at the conjunctiva and nail beds is a quick, classic nursing trick to check if blood color looks healthy and pink! [learn more](GNS226_U4_T009#GNS226_U4_T009_h6)

question: You are about to give an IV antibiotic to your patient. What is the best way to use technology right at that moment?

options.A: Leave the medication at the bedside table while going to find a laptop
options.B: Write the administration time on a piece of paper to type into the desktop computer later
options.C: Scan the patient identification band and the medication label using a handheld device
options.D: Ask a family member to double-check the medication order on the wall chart

explanation: You nailed it! Point-of-care scanning right at the bedside prevents errors and ensures your charting is accurate in real time. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T4#GNS113_U1_T4_h3)

question: What does it usually mean if a patient's deep tendon reflex is very weak or missing entirely?

options.A: Hyperactive function of the spinal cord
options.B: Severe brain injury in the cerebral cortex
options.C: Excessive physical activity of the limb
options.D: Lower motor neuron or peripheral nerve damage

explanation: When a reflex pathway in the limbs is damaged or blocked, the physical response becomes sluggish or disappears. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T25#GNS211_U3_T25_h8)

question: Which nerve fibers send quick, sharp, 'ouch!' pain straight to your brain?

options.A: Autonomic fibers
options.B: C fibers
options.C: A-delta fibers
options.D: Motor neurons

explanation: Great job! A-delta fibers are wrapped in myelin (like an insulated wire), letting them zoom signals to your brain instantly when you get hurt. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T7#GNS221_U3_T7_h2)

question: What is the primary reason FGM continues to be practiced in many Nigerian communities?

options.A: Deeply rooted cultural traditions and beliefs
options.B: Recommendations from international health bodies
options.C: Medical advice given by local physicians
options.D: Treatment for chronic reproductive infections

explanation: FGM persists largely because of long-standing cultural traditions, myths about purity, and social pressure rather than medical necessity. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T7#GNS312_U1_T7_h1)

question: How must strong opioid medications be kept safe on a nursing ward?

options.A: Inside a double-locked secure metal cabinet
options.B: Unsecured in the main treatment preparation room
options.C: Inside the patient's bedside bedside drawer
options.D: On an open shelf near the nurse's main desk

explanation: Controlled substances like opioids are always kept under double locks to prevent theft and ensure they only go to the patients who truly need them. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T4#GNS125_U4_T4_h4)

question: What do we call a community diagnosis that zeroes in on one specific health issue or vulnerable group?

options.A: Randomized clinical diagnosis
options.B: Comprehensive community diagnosis
options.C: Inpatient hospital diagnosis
options.D: Problem-oriented community diagnosis

explanation: Well done! A problem-oriented assessment focuses tightly on a particular issue or group rather than trying to examine everything at once. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T18#GNS225_U2_T18_h3)

question: What does the letter 'M' stand for in the SMART goal framework used in rehabilitation?

options.A: Medical
options.B: Mobile
options.C: Measurable
options.D: Manual

explanation: Goals must be measurable so the healthcare team and the patient can clearly see when a milestone has been reached. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T4#GNS123_U6_T4_h2)

question: Why should you NOT send a patient with a blocked airway for a CT scan right away?

options.A: X-rays cannot show foreign objects at all.
options.B: The scanner is usually too far from the ward.
options.C: Contrast dye makes the vocal cords snap shut.
options.D: Keeping the airway open is always the top emergency priority.

explanation: An unstable airway can close up completely at any second. Saving the patient's life by securing their breathing always comes before moving them for pictures. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T4#GNS213_U2_T4_h5)

question: What happens to blood pressure if small arterioles constrict and become narrower?

options.A: Blood pressure drops to zero
options.B: Blood pressure fluctuates wildly every second
options.C: Blood pressure remains completely unchanged
options.D: Blood pressure increases

explanation: Narrowing the blood vessels increases resistance, which raises the pressure needed to push blood through them. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T12#GNS111_U2_T12_h6)

question: When wrapping a residual limb with an elastic bandage, where should the pressure be tightest?

options.A: At the bottom end of the stump
options.B: Equally tight all the way up
options.C: Near the top of the joint
options.D: Across the middle portion

explanation: Wrapping tighter at the bottom (distal end) pushes fluid upward and helps shape the limb into a neat cone, which makes fitting a prosthesis much easier later. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T12#GNS324_U4_T12_h4)

question: What is the main job of the tiny balloon cuff on an endotracheal tube?

options.A: To pump oxygen automatically into the lungs
options.B: To filter dust from incoming room air
options.C: To measure the patient's blood pressure
options.D: To secure the tube in place and prevent aspiration

explanation: Inflating that little cuff creates a gentle seal inside the windpipe. It keeps the tube firmly in position and blocks stomach contents from slipping into the lungs. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T5#GNS315_U3_T5_h4)

question: A village faces a sudden cholera outbreak and needs quick action. What is an NGO most likely to do first?

question: What is the term for the process of children learning societal gender roles as they grow up?

question: Why do older adults often become dehydrated without even realizing it?

question: An older client with dementia relies totally on her son for baths and medication. Why is she at high risk for abuse?

question: What is the primary function of the musculoskeletal system?

question: What do we call an unexpected injury caused by medical care rather than the patient's actual sickness?

question: Which of these is NOT a major challenge facing sheltered workshops in Nigeria?

question: How is an outbreak different from an epidemic?

question: What physical health issue is very common among child trafficking survivors?

question: A patient only opens their eyes and groans briefly when you press firmly on their fingernail bed. How do we term this state?

question: Why is it important to pick the right statistical test for your research data?

question: What is the main reason behind conduction deafness?

question: Why are patients with weak immune systems at much higher risk after an abortion procedure?

question: Why is it a mistake for a nurse manager to panic over every single normal, everyday variation?

question: What is the only true cure for preeclampsia?

question: A newborn with severe moulding and a large cephalhematoma is in the nursery. Which nursing action is WRONG and unsafe?

question: During the primary survey, a trauma nurse cuts away a patient's heavy jacket. What is the main reason for this action under the 'Exposure' step?

question: Why are regular check-ins necessary during the MBO process?

question: What is the primary clinical role of a family planning record?

question: In healthcare, what does EHR 'interoperability' mean?

question: Why is taking corticosteroids together with NSAIDs (like ibuprofen) a big risk?

question: Why do water quality testers measure turbidity?

question: Legally speaking, what happens if you perform a nursing care action but forget to write it down?

question: Which of these is NOT something you should focus on when writing nursing practice implications?

question: What is the main risk of aggressively stripping surgical drainage tubes?

question: Why are basic averages and percentages not enough on their own for explanatory research?

question: Which of these is a great example of primary prevention in the home?

question: Why is the issue of consent particularly critical when discussing forced marriage?

question: A 45-year-old woman comes to the clinic with a hard, painless breast lump she noticed six months ago. What often causes this kind of late presentation in our communities?

question: How do scientists use bacteria like E. coli in modern recombinant DNA technology?

question: What is the main goal of providing quality reproductive health care?

question: A nurse complains that a new electronic medication system is too confusing and slows her down. What is likely going on?

question: How do tables and bullet points help when writing clinical documents?

question: Which type of memory relies heavily on the basal ganglia?

options.A: Factual memory for historical dates
options.B: Immediate sensory memory for loud noises
options.C: Procedural memory for learned motor skills
options.D: Visual memory for reading text

explanation: Procedural memory is about the things your body learns to do automatically, like riding a bike or writing. These muscle habits rely heavily on the basal ganglia! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T12#GNS211_U3_T12_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of routine spirometry testing in an industrial occupational health clinic?

options.A: To test the employee's hearing capacity against machine noise
options.B: To check if the worker has contracted a stomach ulcer
options.C: To measure the exact body weight and fat percentage of workers
options.D: To detect early drops in lung function before symptoms appear

explanation: Regular spirometry allows nurses and occupational health officers to spot early breathing impairments so corrective safety steps can be taken immediately. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h8)

question: How should a nurse approach a physical assessment for a patient with a history of FGM?

options.A: Perform the examination quickly without discussing the steps to save time.
options.B: Avoid performing any physical examinations to prevent patient anxiety.
options.C: Explain every step gently and proceed with high sensitivity.
options.D: Ask family members to hold the patient still during the assessment.

question: What type of observation happens when a researcher joins a group to experience their daily routine firsthand?

options.A: Non-participant observation
options.B: Participant observation
options.C: Structured observation
options.D: Laboratory observation

question: What should every good IEC material clearly include at the end of its message?

options.A: A detailed biography of the nurse who designed the material
options.B: A specific call to action telling the audience what to do next
options.C: A complete list of medical research references and journal sources
options.D: A complex scientific definition of the disease being discussed

explanation: Always tell your audience what practical step they can take right now to protect their health! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T4#GNS124_U5_T4_h4)

question: Why is it so important to physically clean instruments before disinfecting or sterilizing them?

options.A: To wash away dried blood and tissue that shield germs

options.C: To make the metal look shiny and brand new
options.D: To instantly make the instruments completely sterile

explanation: Spot on! If blood or organic matter is left on an instrument, it acts like a shield protecting germs from the disinfectant. [learn more](GST114_U2_T12#GST114_U2_T12_h6)

question: What is the main goal of Family Life Education?

options.C: Psychiatric medication management for depression
options.D: Emergency trauma care for injured children

explanation: Spot on! Family Life Education is all about teaching healthy habits and preventing issues before they start, rather than treating illnesses or emergencies. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T19#GNS312_U3_T19_h1)
